dish: single-origin espresso flight / New Orleans iced coffee
w: SF's third-wave standard-bearer; the Ferry Building espresso bar is the only Blue Bottle pouring single-origin flights (the original Mint Plaza cafe is now closed).
One of the original SF third-wave roasters; the cavernous Valencia flagship is a Mission daily ritual, cited in Food & Wine's 2026 top U.S. coffee-cities ranking.
Iconic SoMa roastery in a 1914 warehouse open to the rafters; craft light-roast single origins roasted on-site, one of the shops that gave SF its roaster depth.
Mission third-wave roaster (est. 2008) roasting in-house on a vintage German machine; a spare menu that lets the roast talk, with a visible roaster and long communal tables.
Russian Hill/Polk Gulch's sleekest cafe, a Scandi-minimalist counter; the owner's obsessive sourcing from Guatemala, Kenya and Honduras and its housemade nut milk draw the coffee crowd.

dish: Snowy Plover (espresso, brown-sugar, sparkling water, Bailey's whipped cream)
w: Outer Sunset roaster-bakery (est. 2014); the signature Snowy Plover is a foggy-day icon of the neighborhood coffee scene.
Cow Hollow micro-cafe from Trish Rothgeb — the roaster who literally coined 'third wave coffee' — and Nicholas Cho; pineapple-wallpaper #pineappleselfie spot with a custom pour-over bar.

dish: themed seasonal cocktail menu (menu changes biannually)
w: Mission cocktail landmark whose art-object menus reinvent around a theme (Pantone colors, astrology, records); a World's 50 Best Bars regular and top-ranked U.S. bar.

dish: tiki rum cocktail served in a fresh coconut
w: Hayes Valley tiki temple with the largest rum selection in the U.S. (1,300+) and 80 cocktails; six-time World's 50 Best Bars listee and once Tales of the Cocktail's best U.S. bar.

dish: the namesake Bourbon & Branch / classic cocktails
w: Tenderloin Prohibition-era speakeasy in a real 1920s bar space; password-and-buzzer entry, five secret rooms, and the walk-in Library behind a bookcase — a trailblazer of SF's cocktail revival.
North Beach's last standing Barbary Coast bar (1907), original mahogany bar and punkah fans; well-dressed bartenders, live jazz and a Free Lunch Friday tradition.

dish: seasonal craft cocktails (and a top-tier late-night burger)
w: Mission bar from Bourbon & Branch/Beretta alumni — cocktails several steps above the norm in an unpretentious room, with one of the best burgers in the city until midnight.

dish: foraged/fermented cocktails with elevated bar bites
w: Mission cocktail bar from the Michelin-starred Lazy Bear team; inventive drinks using fermented honey and roasted quince, and North America's 50 Best 'most sustainable bar'.
Award-winning Union Square bar led by local legend Kevin Diedrich; Asian-Pacific-driven drinks that landed it at #16 on North America's 50 Best Bars.
Inner Richmond bakery named Bon Appetit's Bakery of the Year; preposterously flaky, brioche-tender croissants that draw a daily line — widely called SF's best.
Lower Pac Heights French patisserie from James Beard-winning pastry chef Belinda Leong; the caramel-crusted kouign-amann is considered among the country's best.
Outer Sunset beach-side bakery selling 500-600 breakfast sandwiches a weekend — egg, pepper jack, bacon, avocado and lemon-garlic aioli on a buttermilk biscuit; pillowy $1 Sunday beignets.
